No View Is the Whole

The World and the Ways We Make Sense of It

Soman Lin

The book opens on a handful of scenes far apart from one another: a horse in Berlin that seemed to do arithmetic; a physician in London in 1854 asking door to door which pump the dead had drunk from; an autopilot over the Atlantic handing control back to two co-pilots; a computer alarm on the lunar lander that nobody had yet traced; a priest under the ruined Rashomon gate handing a child to a woodcutter whose story had already changed once.

They point at one question: how the way we make sense of the world is itself formed, who can check it, and how it is handed on to the next person. The author calls the turn of counting oneself in “the second realisation”, and closes with a claim about long-term reliance: when choosing a method, weigh how it will shape the evidence, learning and correction available later.

Fifteen chapters in four parts, seventeen figures, seventy-five sources you can check. Chinese and English, switchable inside the reader.

所見非全貌

世界，以及我們理解它的方式

Soman Lin

這本書從幾個相隔很遠的場面開始：柏林一匹似乎會算術的馬；一八五四年的倫敦，一位醫師逐戶追問死者喝的是哪一口井的水；大西洋上空，自動駕駛把操縱權交還給兩名副駕駛；月球軌道上，登月小艇的電腦發出還沒有人查清原因的警報；破敗的羅生門下，僧人把一個孩子交給說法已經改過一次的樵夫。

它們指向同一個問題：我們用來理解世界的那套眼光，本身是怎樣形成的，能被誰檢查，又怎樣傳給下一個人。作者把「把自己也算進去」的轉變稱為「第二次頓悟」，並在全書最後提出一項評價長期依賴的主張：選用一種方法時，也要看它如何影響往後取得證據、學習與修正錯誤的能力。

全書十五章分成四部，十七組圖，七十五條可回查的來源註。中英雙語，可在閱讀器內切換。
